name: Greenroom
note: Skipped 2026-08-03 after investigation. Wix Stores. The site sitemap lists six pages and no products; there is no /store-products-sitemap.xml either, so products are not discoverable by crawling. Reaching them needs Wix's storefront catalog API, which requires first pulling an anonymous token from /_api/v1/access-tokens — close enough to the 'needs a login/token' line in the adapter playbook that it is not worth crossing for a brand this size. The /products/ link on their homepage goes to gordongreenroom.com, which is a partner site and 404s on products.json.

name: Troubadour
note: troubadourgoods.com is a headless Next.js storefront on Vercel using Shopify's URL shapes, which is why the feed read as bad_json: /products.json there returns the app shell. The underlying store is troubadour.myshopify.com and answers Shopify's own local_rate_limited, which is this IP's block rather than their configuration — a non-Shopify host could not produce that response. Unverified from here for exactly that reason; it will prove itself on the next Actions run.

name: CampSaver
note: Retired 2026-08-02. A retailer, not a brand: it has yielded 0 models across every run, and the aggregator:direct-source-exists rule exists to reject its products wherever the brand is already sourced directly — so a successful crawl mostly produces duplicates of catalogues we hold first-hand. It is also soft-blocked behind behavioural bot protection that answers 200 with a forbidden.html, and it was occupying a whole shard to contribute nothing. The adapter stays in fetch.py; only this entry is retired.

name: CamelBak
note: Retired 2026-08-02. Measured at 10.3 min a run for 16 models (16 with dimensions) — see the roster section of the handoff. Too slow for the return, and not a brand this audience is looking for. normalize.py globs raw/ and never reads this file, so the catalogue already fetched stays in the index; only the refetch stops, and validate.py exempts retired entries from the freshness check so it goes stale deliberately rather than by neglect.

name: Vaude
note: Retired 2026-08-04. Measured at 40.1 min for 303 products on the 2026-08-03 run — 30% of the entire night's crawl time for one brand, and 7.9 s/product against a feed brand's 0.3. The cost is the Magento GraphQL adapter paging a product at a time, not the pacing, so no DELAY change recovers it. normalize.py globs raw/ and never reads this file, so the 292 models already fetched stay in the index; only the refetch stops, and validate.py exempts retired entries from the freshness check so it goes stale deliberately rather than by neglect. The "magento" platform above is what raw/vaude.json still records and what normalize reads; restore it here to turn the crawl back on.
